ACBPR.description: Defines an Access Class Barring profile, specifying which access classes (AC0-AC15 groups) are barred, for how long, and with what probability factor, including special exceptions for MMTEL voice/video and SMS. It is referenced by cell system information (SIB) configuration to control which UEs are permitted to attempt RRC connection during congestion.

threeGpp.note: Access Class Barring is broadcast via SIB2's ac-BarringInfo, a 3GPP-defined RRC structure.

Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

ADJS.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "ADJS". It did not appear in the researched sample set. ALARMSUPP.description: ALARMSUPP defines alarm and fault suppression rules for the BTS/gNB, letting operators specify lists of allowed/suppressed alarm and fault IDs and severities so that specific alarms are muted (e.g. during planned maintenance or for known non-actionable conditions). It is a site-level operations-and-maintenance configuration object.

threeGpp.note: Site-wide Nokia O&M/administrative configuration, not part of any 3GPP-defined model.

ALD.description: ALD (Antenna Line Device) represents a generic RET or TMA (Tower-Mounted Amplifier) device controlled over the antenna interface (typically AISG protocol), identified by its control protocol, product code, and serial number. It is the general antenna-line accessory object that RETU and TMA-specific objects build upon.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

ALD_R.description: ALD_R is the resource/state counterpart of ALD, reporting the antenna line device's availability, operational, and procedural status alongside its control-protocol and hardware identification fields.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

AMGR.description: Configures centralized account/authentication management for the BTS, including LDAP server connectivity, restricted local-access policy, and password-complexity rules, supporting integration with an external corporate LDAP/AAA directory. It works alongside LUAC (local account policy) to govern operator access to the element.

AMLEPR.description: Defines a mobility/load-balancing profile per target carrier frequency, specifying call-admission-control (CAC) headroom and threshold values used by an adaptive mobility load-balancing feature to decide when UEs should be steered toward that frequency layer. The precise feature name behind the 'AMLE' abbreviation is uncertain, but the parameters clearly tie it to inter-frequency, load-based mobility control.

threeGpp.note: Frequency-layer prioritization for idle-mode reselection is broadcast via standardized SIB IEs (TS 36.331), but this specific mobility/load-balancing decision profile and its thresholds are Nokia's own algorithm.

ANR.description: The Automatic Neighbor Relation function object for an LTE cell/eNodeB, controlling automatic addition and removal of neighbor relations (LTE, NR, UTRAN) based on measurement thresholds, inactivity timers, and guard periods, minimizing manual neighbor list engineering. It works together with ANRPRL profiles to define per-frequency thresholds.

threeGpp.note: This IS the Automatic Neighbor Relation function the spec is named for.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Automatic Neighbour Relation (ANR) management; Concepts and requirements

ANRPRL.description: Defines an Automatic Neighbor Relation (ANR) profile per target carrier frequency, specifying the RSRP/RSRQ thresholds a candidate neighbor cell must exceed before being added as a confirmed neighbor, plus limits on how many inter-frequency/intra-frequency neighbors ANR may add. It works together with the ANR function object to automate neighbor relation discovery and pruning.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Automatic Neighbour Relation (ANR) management; Concepts and requirements

ANRPRW.description: An Automatic Neighbor Relation (ANR) profile specific to UTRAN (3G/WCDMA) neighbors, defining the Ec/No and RSCP detection thresholds used to qualify a detected 3G cell as a valid neighbor, RNC-ID coding/type/alignment settings for building the target cell identity, and flags controlling PS handover, CSFB-to-PS handover, and SRVCC toward that UTRAN neighbor. It governs how the LTE cell automatically builds and manages its list of 3G neighbor relations.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Automatic Neighbour Relation (ANR) management; Concepts and requirements

ANTL.description: An Antenna Line Device object representing RF line equipment mounted at or near the antenna, such as a Remote Electrical Tilt (RET) actuator or Tower-Mounted Amplifier (TMA), typically controlled over AISG-style signaling. Its parameters cover antenna port mapping, uplink/downlink path delay calibration, timing advance, and receiver sensitivity, and it sits under a CABINET/APEQM branch, linked to the radio module via a CABLINK.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

ANTL_R.description: The runtime/inventory counterpart to the ANTL configuration object, reporting the live operational and administrative state of an antenna line device (RET/TMA), including measured antenna path delays, VSWR alarm thresholds, and TX/RX capability flags. It reflects actual detected hardware status rather than planned configuration.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

APEQM.description: The Auto Plug-and-Play Equipment root object, under which automatically discovered hardware is organized before or as it is commissioned. Its parameters include scanning intervals and alarm thresholds (BER, eCPRI timing window) related to the auto-discovery and monitoring process, plus SFP operating mode.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

APEQM_R.description: APEQM_R is the resource-side root of the auto-discovery/plug-and-play equipment subtree, controlling (via aldScanningInterval) how often the system scans for newly connected antenna line devices (RET/TMA) to auto-detect and register them.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

APUCCH_FDD.description: The FDD counterpart to APUCCH_TDD, configuring adaptive/dynamic PUCCH resource allocation (handover reservation thresholds, minimum RRC/emergency session reservations, PRACH frequency offset, CSI report format) for an FDD LTE cell.
APUCCH_FDD.officialFullName: Automatic PUCCH Allocation Configuration for FDD Cell

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PUCCH-Config information element.

APUCCH_TDD.description: Configures the adaptive (dynamic) PUCCH (Physical Uplink Control Channel) resource allocation algorithm for a TDD LTE cell, including thresholds for adding PUCCH resources on handover, minimum reserved resources for emergency/RRC sessions, and PRACH frequency offset assignment. It lets the eNodeB dynamically size PUCCH capacity based on load rather than using a fixed allocation.
APUCCH_TDD.officialFullName: Automatic PUCCH Allocation Configuration for TDD Cell

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PUCCH-Config information element.

BBADM.description: A baseband administration object under the site management-network-layer (mnl) branch, used to hold administrative settings or actions related to baseband module management (such as activation, decommissioning, or capacity administration). No sample parameters were captured in this dataset, so its exact scope is inferred mainly from its name and namespace.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

BBMOD.description: Represents a Baseband Module (BBU) - the hardware unit performing digital baseband processing (channel coding, modulation, scheduling) for LTE and/or NR cells. Parameters cover administrative state, baseband pool sizing and usage, board configuration type, and FDD/NR cell configuration tradeoffs, and it sits under a CABINET/APEQM branch, connected to radio modules via CABLINK.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

BBMOD_R.description: A runtime/status mirror of the baseband module (BBMOD) hardware object, reporting administrative and operational state, availability status, and inventory details (product code/name, board product code, serial numbers) of a baseband processing module. Fields such as eutraSupport, geranSupport, and nrSupport indicate which radio access technologies the board's hardware can process. It lives in the equipment hardware tree beneath the BBU/system module, reflecting live hardware-discovery data for a baseband unit.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

BBPOOL.description: Represents a baseband resource pool that groups multiple baseband hardware units/power groups (bbPwrGroupDNList) and lists the cells sharing that pooled baseband capacity (bbPoolCellsList) for a given radio technology (bbPoolTech). This supports Nokia's baseband pooling/capacity-sharing feature, letting several cells dynamically share processing resources across baseband modules, and sits under the equipment/baseband management branch.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

BBPOOLALLOC.description: Configures how baseband processing capacity is allocated to a cell or function from a shared baseband resource pool, specifying the allocation mode and the hosting baseband/physical pool IDs. It is part of Nokia's baseband pooling architecture that lets multiple cells share BBMOD processing capacity flexibly.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

BFDGRP.description: Represents a Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) group used to configure fast failure detection for one or more transport-layer paths or routes. It groups related BFD sessions for management purposes within the transport network configuration; it carries no directly sampled parameters in this dataset.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IETF (RFC 5880, BFD), not 3GPP. Fast link-failure detection, unrelated to 3GPP.

BRGPRT.description: Represents a Layer-2 bridge port associated with an underlying Ethernet link (via ethlkDN), configuring VLAN membership/default VLAN, ingress frame-type acceptance, and traffic-shaping parameters (burst size, shaper rate) for that port within the internal Ethernet switch fabric. It works alongside ETHLK and L2SWI to build the site's internal Layer-2 switching topology.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

BTOOTH.description: BTOOTH configures the Bluetooth radio interface built into some AirScale/Flexi Zone modules, used for short-range local commissioning and maintenance access (e.g. from a technician's tablet). Parameters control whether Bluetooth is enabled, device name, pairing modes (legacy vs. Secure Simple Pairing) and their shared secrets, inquiry/scan response behavior, and pairing-relationship timers.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

BWP_PROFILE.description: Defines a 5G NR Bandwidth Part (BWP) profile, specifying its type and the common resource block start/size for uplink and downlink (or the encoded locationAndBandwidth value). BWPs let an NR cell allocate different frequency-domain resource regions to UEs, and this profile is referenced by NR cell/UE configuration.

threeGpp.note: Bandwidth Parts are defined via the RRC BWP-Downlink/BWP-Uplink information elements.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

CABINET.description: Represents a physical cabinet or outdoor enclosure housing BTS hardware modules. Its parameters (temperature sensor readings and high-temperature alarm threshold) reflect its role in environmental monitoring of the equipment it contains, and it sits under EQM/APEQM as the parent of modules such as SMOD, BBMOD, and RMOD.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

CABINET_R.description: CABINET_R is the resource/state object for a physical cabinet or enclosure, recording inventory details (product code, product name, serial number) and a configuration-object reference (configDN) linking back to the corresponding CABINET configuration object.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

CABLINK.description: Represents a physical fronthaul/interconnect cable (e.g. a CPRI or eCPRI fiber link) between two hardware endpoints, identified by their distinguished names and port IDs, along with configured link speed, radio protocol type, and IQ compression mode. It is commonly used to model the link between a baseband module (BBMOD) and a radio module (RMOD).

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

CABLINK_R.description: CABLINK_R is the resource/state object for a physical fiber or copper cable link (commonly a CPRI/eCPRI fronthaul link) connecting a baseband module to a radio module, reporting availability/operational status, fiber length, link speed, IQ compression setting, and which functions (data, synchronization, DC power) the link mode carries. The '_R' suffix marks it as the runtime state counterpart to the equipment's cabling configuration, sitting under the equipment (eqmr) branch of the hierarchy.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

CACERT_R.description: CACERT_R is a resource object representing a trusted CA (Certificate Authority) certificate installed in the BTS/gNB's PKI trust store, recording standard X.509 fields such as issuer, subject, validity period, serial number, key identifiers, signature algorithm, and trust chain. It supports certificate-based authentication used for IPsec, TLS, and CMP enrollment.

CADPR.description: A Carrier Aggregation deployment/decision profile for LTE, defining the A3/A6 measurement-event thresholds, time-to-trigger, and hysteresis used to decide when to add or swap a secondary component carrier (SCell), along with limits on MIMO layers per duplex mode and maximum SCell swaps. It is a feature-configuration object referenced by an LTE cell to govern its carrier-aggregation behavior rather than a physical or radio object itself.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

CADPRCBRS.description: A Carrier Aggregation deployment profile variant specific to CBRS-band secondary cells, defining the A3/A6 event thresholds, time-to-trigger, hysteresis, RSRP/RSRQ measurement thresholds (scellMeasThreshRsrp/Rsrq), and frequency priority used when deciding whether to add a CBRS-band SCell via carrier aggregation. It mirrors CADPR but is tailored to the constraints of shared CBRS spectrum.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

CADPRLAA.description: A Carrier Aggregation deployment profile variant for LAA (unlicensed-band) secondary cells, defining A3/A6 measurement-event thresholds and hysteresis, frequency priority including a DFS-specific priority (sFreqPrioDfs), and RSRP measurement thresholds used when deciding whether to add an LAA SCell via carrier aggregation. It mirrors CADPR/CADPRCBRS but is tailored to LAA unlicensed-spectrum SCells.
CADPRLAA.officialFullName: Carrier Aggregation Default Profile for License-Assisted Access

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

CAGENB.description: CAGENB configures inter-eNB Carrier Aggregation cluster behavior, listing the group of eNodeBs (caClusterEnbList, referenced by lnBtsId) that participate together in cross-node carrier aggregation, plus related CA scheduling parameters -- SCell scheduling weight based on minimum CQI, fast load-balancing thresholds, uplink pathloss-based SCell activation offsets/thresholds, PRB usage thresholds, and SRIO link counts used for inter-baseband coordination.

threeGpp.note: Carrier Aggregation itself, and its RRC-signalled measurement/configuration IEs, are 3GPP-standardized (see also TS 36.300 for the overall CA description); this specific profile/decision object is Nokia's own OAM wrapper around those standardized IEs.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

CAIMLBP.description: Configures the Primary Cell (PCell) side of a carrier-aggregation-related inter-frequency mobility/load-balancing feature, specifying the downlink EARFCN of the candidate PCell frequency layer (earfcnDL) and a reference to its cell configuration (pcellConfig). It works together with CAIMLBS (the SCell counterpart) to define candidate frequency layers for CA-aware mobility load balancing.
CAIMLBP.officialFullName: Carrier Aggregation Idle Mode LB Configuration For PCells

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

CAIMLBS.description: The Secondary Cell (SCell) counterpart to CAIMLBP, specifying the downlink EARFCN of a candidate SCell frequency layer (earfcnDL), a reference to its cell configuration (scellConfig), and the maximum number of SCells allowed (maxNumScells) for carrier-aggregation-aware inter-frequency mobility/load-balancing decisions.
CAIMLBS.officialFullName: Carrier Aggregation Idle Mode LB Configuration For SCells

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

CAPCFG.description: Represents the BTS's baseband capacity/licensing configuration, reporting the current baseband capacity usage of the eNodeB (enbBbCapacityUsage), the hardware release level (enbHwRelease), and which cells have IQ-compression/data-sharing (iqcDs) features applied. It is used to track and report available versus consumed baseband processing capacity.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

CAPR.description: CAPR (Carrier Aggregation Profile) configures the A3/A6 measurement-event parameters (offset, hysteresis, time-to-trigger, reporting interval) used to trigger and manage secondary cell (SCell) addition and SCell swapping for LTE carrier aggregation, along with the DL EARFCN, frequency-priority settings, RSRP threshold for SCell measurement, and the maximum number of SCell swaps allowed.

threeGpp.note: Carrier Aggregation itself, and its RRC-signalled measurement/configuration IEs, are 3GPP-standardized (see also TS 36.300 for the overall CA description); this specific profile/decision object is Nokia's own OAM wrapper around those standardized IEs.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

CAREL.description: Defines a Carrier Aggregation relation between an LTE primary cell (PCell) and a candidate secondary cell (SCell), including whether PCell swapping and SCell beamforming are allowed, the SCell's selection priority, and its downlink scheduling weight factor. It is used to configure which cells may be aggregated together for a UE and how they are prioritized.

threeGpp.note: Carrier Aggregation itself, and its RRC-signalled measurement/configuration IEs, are 3GPP-standardized (see also TS 36.300 for the overall CA description); this specific profile/decision object is Nokia's own OAM wrapper around those standardized IEs.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

CATMPR.description: A large feature-configuration profile for LTE Cat-M1/eMTC (enhanced Machine-Type Communication / LTE-M IoT), covering link-adaptation step sizes and MCS deltas per coverage-enhancement mode (amcCStepUpModeACatM, amcDeltaC.../iniMcsDl/UlModeACatM), HARQ retransmission limits for Msg3/downlink/uplink, RRC connection inactivity timer, default paging cycle, and per-coverage-level (Cat-M CE Level) behavior. It fully parameterizes how the cell serves Cat-M/eMTC IoT devices across normal and extended coverage.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

CBRSCERTH.description: CBRSCERTH controls certificate-handling behavior specific to CBRS (Citizens Broadband Radio Service) operation, notably whether the BTS downloads the SAS PKI's Certificate Revocation List (CRL), which is required to validate the certificate chain used for authenticating with the Spectrum Access System.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

CBRSPR.description: Defines a CBRS (Citizens Broadband Radio Service, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum, band 48) Spectrum Access System (SAS) connection profile, including the primary/secondary SAS server addresses, HTTPS proxy, certificate-management method and TLS settings, WInnForum protocol version (wINNFTSVersion), and supported channel bandwidths. It governs how the BTS, acting as a CBSD, registers with and obtains spectrum grants from a SAS.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

CBSD.description: CBSD represents a CBRS-band (Citizens Broadband Radio Service) radio device registration, holding the antenna's physical characteristics (azimuth, beamwidth, downtilt, gain, model), the FCC ID and device serial number, call sign, and CBRS-specific identifiers (assigned CBSD ID, frequency type, PAL/GAA group IDs) and operating state needed to register with and request spectrum grants from a Spectrum Access System (SAS).

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

CBSDCEL.description: CBSDCEL holds the CBRS (Citizens Broadband Radio Service, US 3.5GHz shared spectrum) SAS-related parameters for an individual LTE cell operating as a CBSD (Citizens Broadband radio Service Device), including desired/fallback TDD frame and subframe configuration, desired maximum power for different channel bandwidths, PRACH frequency offsets, and CQI resource block counts. It complements the base LNCEL cell object for LTE cells deployed in the US CBRS band and works together with the CBSD device object to request spectrum grants from the SAS.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

CDFIM.description: CDFIM configures Access Class Barring (ACB) for an LTE cell per 3GPP TS 36.331 -- separate barring factors/probabilities for Access Classes 0-9 (with an adaptive/overload variant) and Access Classes 10-15 (each with its own overload variant) -- used to control which categories of UEs are barred from initiating RRC connection establishment during congestion or overload conditions.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

CELLMAPPING.description: Has no configurable parameters of its own; it functions as a mapping/association container, most likely linking logical cell objects to the physical or baseband hardware resources (e.g. a baseband pool or specific RF module) that serve them.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

CERTH.description: Configures certificate lifecycle management for the BTS, including CRL distribution point/usage, CMP (Certificate Management Protocol) server address and polling settings, and automatic certificate/CA renewal and deletion behavior. It underlies the PKI-based security used for secure O&M, TLS, and IPsec connections.

CERTHENT.description: A sub-entry of the certificate-handling configuration that associates a specific source IPv4 address (via cmpCrlSrcIpv4AddressDN) with CMP/CRL traffic, likely used when the BTS has multiple IP interfaces and must pin certificate-management traffic to a particular source address.

CHANNEL.description: Represents a logical signal channel (e.g. an uplink or downlink RET/TMA control channel) belonging to an antenna line device, referenced back to its parent via antlDN, with a direction attribute indicating its role. It is a low-level equipment object used to model the individually controllable channels of an antenna line device such as a RET motor or tower-mounted amplifier, typically sitting as a child of an ANTL object.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

CHANNELGROUP.description: Groups multiple CHANNEL objects together for collective configuration or reporting, likely representing a bank of RET/TMA control channels on a single antenna line device. It has no directly configurable parameters of its own and functions mainly as an organizational container.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

CLOCK.description: Configures the clock/timing distribution settings of a system module (SMOD), including which synchronization inputs (1PPS, 2M048, PDH, backplane, fronthaul-slave) are accepted, their priority order, whether the module acts as sync master, and total delay compensation from the site's synchronization hub module. It is a child of an SMOD and central to the site's timing/frequency synchronization chain.

CLOCK_FDD.description: Configures the BTS's synchronization clock behavior for FDD (Frequency Division Duplex) operation, specifically whether this unit acts as the synchronization master (syncMaster) in the timing distribution scheme. It is the FDD counterpart to CLOCK_TDD.

CLOCK_R.description: CLOCK_R is the resource/state object for the node's synchronization clock subsystem, reporting the currently active synchronization mode and time source (e.g. GNSS, SyncE, PTP), which sync input is currently selected, whether SyncE-assisted handover mode is in use, and automatically detected cable/link delay. It reflects the runtime outcome of the STPG/TOP/GNSSI synchronization configuration.

CLOCK_TDD.description: Configures the BTS's synchronization clock behavior specifically for TDD (Time Division Duplex) operation, including whether the unit acts as a synchronization slave in a dual-mode (FDD+TDD) deployment (dualModeSyncSlave). It is part of the timing/synchronization subsystem that works alongside GNSS/PTP/SyncE sources to keep TDD cells frame-aligned.

CMASPRIO.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "CMASPRIO". It did not appear in the researched sample set. Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

CMD.description: Has no configurable parameters and appears to represent a command/action trigger object, likely used to invoke management operations such as resets or diagnostics, rather than persistent configuration.

CMP.description: Configures the Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) client used by the BTS to automatically enroll and renew its PKI certificates, including the CMP server path/port, certificate validation behavior, key length, and CA/certificate update scheduling.

CMPECDSA.description: CMPECDSA configures automatic certificate enrollment/renewal via the Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) using ECDSA key pairs, including the CMP server address/port/type, polling timeout, key length, and certificate update timestamps for both the CA and the network element's own certificate. It is a security object supporting PKI-based mutual authentication (e.g. for IPsec/TLS) on the BTS/gNB.

CMPECDSA_R.description: A runtime status object tracking a Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) enrollment operation that uses ECDSA (elliptic-curve) key/signature algorithms, recording the current enrollment state and the target certificate's distinguished name (targetDN). It is the ECDSA-specific counterpart to CMP_R.

CMPFH.description: CMPFH configures Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) enrollment specifically for the fronthaul interface, tracking the CA and network-element certificate key length and update timestamps used to secure fronthaul connections (e.g. between DU and RU) with PKI-issued certificates. It parallels the general CMPECDSA object but is scoped to fronthaul security.

CMPFHEXT.description: CMPFHEXT extends CMPFH with X.509 extended-key-usage settings (TLS client authentication and TLS server authentication flags) used when requesting fronthaul security certificates, controlling what the issued certificate may be used for.

L2SWI.description: Represents a Layer-2 switch interface configuration, controlling DSCP-to-queue mapping, layer-2 QoS/switching enablement, and priority-queue weighting (including weighted-fair-queuing weights for assured-forwarding classes). It underlies the BTS's internal Ethernet switch fabric QoS behavior.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

LAA.description: Configures the LAA (License Assisted Access) feature, which lets an LTE cell opportunistically use unlicensed 5 GHz spectrum as a supplemental downlink carrier via carrier aggregation. Parameters cover Listen-Before-Talk clear-channel-assessment thresholds (ccaThresholdXr), a frequency hold-off timer after a channel becomes busy, an SCell-release timer tied to interference detection (idcLaaScellReleaseTimer), dynamic power control (DPC) evaluation/kickdown timers, and the applicable ITU region for regulatory rules (lteUItuRegion).

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

LANE.description: Represents an individual Ethernet lane/port on a switch or interface module, exposing its administrative state (administrativeState). It is an equipment-level object representing a physical port that can be independently enabled or disabled, distinct from its logical IP/Ethernet-link configuration.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

LANE_R.description: LANE_R is a resource object representing an individual physical/logical 'lane' within a multi-lane interface (such as a CPRI/eCPRI fronthaul link or a multi-lane optical/electrical interconnect), reporting only its operational state. It is a fine-grained equipment status object beneath a link or port object.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

LBPUCCHRDPR.description: Defines a load-based PUCCH resource reduction profile, specifying RRC-connected-UE thresholds and countdown timers used to dynamically compress or expand PUCCH capacity as cell load changes. It works together with the adaptive PUCCH (APUCCH) configuration to balance control-channel capacity against uplink data capacity under varying load.
LBPUCCHRDPR.officialFullName: Load Based PUCCH Region Default PRofile

threeGpp.note: Built on top of standardized concepts (PUCCH resource config / transmission mode, TS 36.331 and TS 36.213 respectively), but the load-based decision logic and thresholds in this specific profile are Nokia's own algorithm, not something 3GPP specifies.

LBPUCCHRPR.description: A load-based PUCCH resource-adaptation profile, defining upper/lower thresholds of RRC-connected UE count that trigger expansion or contraction of PUCCH control-channel resources, along with countdown timers used to smooth those expansion/compression transitions (countdownPucchCompr/Expr). It helps the eNodeB dynamically balance PUCCH capacity against PUSCH data capacity as cell load changes.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

LCELL.description: Appears to be a site- or cell-level container for cross-RAT radio spectrum-sharing feature toggles, such as dynamic LTE/WCDMA shared spectrum operation and distributed-antenna-system MIMO activation. Its exact scope is not fully certain from the parameter set alone, but it groups spectrum-sharing controls rather than per-cell radio resource parameters.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

LCELNR.description: LCELNR appears to link an LTE cell's configuration to 5G NR interworking features, based on its parameter names referencing antenna-sharing/distributed-MIMO with NR (actAsiDistMimoNr) and simplified channel configuration for massive-MIMO active antennas (actSimplChConfMAA). It likely toggles LTE/NR active-antenna-sharing feature behavior for a cell involved in dynamic spectrum sharing or shared-antenna deployments.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

LLOCK.description: Implements a 'location lock'/site-movement-detection feature that monitors whether the BTS has been physically relocated or tampered with, using GNSS position drift (gnssTriggerDistance) and/or detection of unexpected neighbor cells (detectionMethods, minimumNumberOfNeighbors, neighborsDetectionTime) as triggers, with a configurable alarming period and automatic-disable behavior. It is a site-integrity/self-protection feature-configuration object rather than a radio or hardware object.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

LNADJ.description: Defines a classic X2 neighbor relation from an LTE cell to another LTE eNodeB, storing the target eNB's ID, PLMN identity, control-plane IP address, and whether RLF-based (Radio Link Failure) reconfiguration/reporting is supported toward that neighbor (rlfBasedRCRsupported). It is the LTE-to-LTE counterpart of LNADJGNB and underlies X2-based handovers between eNodeBs.

threeGpp.note: LTE-to-LTE neighbor relations are governed by the ANR management spec (TS 32.511) and configured/signalled via TS 36.331's mobility IEs.

LNADJGNB.description: Defines a neighbor relation from an LTE cell/eNB to an external 5G gNB, used to support EN-DC (E-UTRAN-NR Dual Connectivity). It stores the target gNB's global ID, PLMN identity (mcc/mnc), control-plane IP address, and the operational status of the X2 link toward that gNB (x2ToGnbLinkStatus). It sits under the LTE BTS's mobility/neighbor configuration and is a prerequisite for adding NR secondary cells to LTE UEs.

threeGpp.note: LTE-NR (EN-DC) neighbor relations are governed by the multi-connectivity spec (TS 37.340), with ANR concepts from TS 32.511 also applying.

LNADJL.description: LNADJL defines an adjacent (neighbor) LTE cell relation, identifying the target cell by its PLMN identity list, ECGI, downlink EARFCN, physical cell ID (PCI), and tracking area code (TAC). It is used by mobility procedures (handover and idle-mode reselection) to describe LTE neighbor cells of a serving LNCEL, part of the LNADJ/LNADJL/LNADJX/LNREL family of neighbor-relation objects.

threeGpp.note: LTE-to-LTE neighbor relations are governed by the ANR management spec (TS 32.511) and configured/signalled via TS 36.331's mobility IEs.

LNADJX.description: Defines an adjacency (neighbor cell) relation from an LTE cell to an external CDMA2000 (1x) cell, identified by band class, PN offset, and sector/market IDs rather than 3GPP cell identifiers. It supports legacy inter-RAT mobility toward 1x networks (e.g. measurement reporting or CS fallback) and is configured as a child relation object under an LNCEL.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by 3GPP2 (a separate standards body for CDMA2000, not part of 3GPP), not 3GPP. CDMA2000 1xRTT/1xEV-DO air-interface parameters are specified in 3GPP2's own C.S00xx document series, entirely outside 3GPP's remit.

LNBTS.description: Represents the logical LTE eNodeB (BTS) function of the site - the parent object under MRBTS for all LTE-specific configuration (cells, neighbor relations, MME connections, mobility, and radio features). It holds an extremely large number of eNodeB-wide 'act*' feature-activation and behavior parameters governing carrier aggregation, access barring, SRVCC, and dozens of other LTE features.

threeGpp.note: Corresponds to the E-UTRAN NRM's ENBFunction IOC.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN) Network Resource Model (NRM) Integration Reference Point (IRP); Information Service (IS)

LNBTS_FDD.description: LNBTS_FDD is the Flexi Zone (NOKLTE) logical LTE FDD eNodeB object -- the parent BTS-level object for one or more LNCEL_FDD cells -- hosting eNB-wide feature-activation toggles spanning VoLTE/SRVCC support, dual-band operation, flexible baseband usage, LAA (License Assisted Access) coexistence and dynamic power control, high-priority service handling, and inter-frequency service-based handover. It sits directly under MRBTS in the site hierarchy.

threeGpp.note: Corresponds to the E-UTRAN NRM's ENBFunction IOC.

LNBTS_TDD.description: The TD-LTE-specific companion object to LNBTS, holding eNodeB-wide feature-activation parameters that apply only to TDD deployments, such as CBRS support, handover to TD-SCDMA, and TDD-specific voice and interference-shaping features. It is instantiated alongside LNBTS for TD-LTE sites.

threeGpp.note: Corresponds to the E-UTRAN NRM's ENBFunction IOC.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN) Network Resource Model (NRM) Integration Reference Point (IRP); Information Service (IS)

LNCEL.description: Represents an LTE cell (FDD or TDD) - the fundamental logical radio cell object of an eNodeB, under which the vast majority of LTE radio resource management, mobility, and feature parameters are configured (hundreds of distinct parameters spanning measurement events, handover thresholds, and redirection behavior). It sits under an LNBTS object and is the parent for cell-specific child objects such as LNREL, SIB, DRX, and PUCCH configuration.

threeGpp.note: The class itself corresponds to the E-UTRAN NRM's EUtranCellFDD/TDD IOC (TS 28.658); most of its individual RRC-facing parameters (SIB content, mobility thresholds, PUCCH/PDCCH config, etc.) are themselves specified in TS 36.331.

LNCEL_FDD.description: LNCEL_FDD is the LTE FDD-mode cell managed object (the Flexi Zone/NOKLTE-namespace counterpart to the AirScale LNCEL class), representing a single LTE FDD cell's radio configuration. With over a hundred parameters it governs numerous cell-level feature activations and radio behaviors -- MIMO modes (including Massive MIMO), carrier types (donut/liquid/slim cell), PUCCH allocation strategy, CAT-M support, and O-RAN interface activation. It sits under an LNBTS (logical eNodeB) object in the site hierarchy.

threeGpp.note: The class itself corresponds to the E-UTRAN NRM's EUtranCellFDD/TDD IOC (TS 28.658); most of its individual RRC-facing parameters (SIB content, mobility thresholds, PUCCH/PDCCH config, etc.) are themselves specified in TS 36.331.

LNCEL_TDD.description: The TDD-specific extension/companion object to LNCEL, holding a very large set of TD-LTE physical-layer and radio-resource parameters (advanced beamforming, MU-MIMO, adaptive PRB allocation for retransmissions, high-speed UE handling, etc.) that apply only to TDD cells. It is instantiated together with the base LNCEL object for TD-LTE cells.

threeGpp.note: The class itself corresponds to the E-UTRAN NRM's EUtranCellFDD/TDD IOC (TS 28.658); most of its individual RRC-facing parameters (SIB content, mobility thresholds, PUCCH/PDCCH config, etc.) are themselves specified in TS 36.331.

LNHENB.description: Configures parameters used to detect and handle Home eNodeBs (HeNBs/femtocells) as potential neighbors of a macro LTE cell, including the PCI range to scan (pciFirst/pciLast), the carrier frequency to search (freqEutra), the cell individual offset to apply, and the eNB-ID size used when decoding the detected HeNB's identity. It supports macro-to-femto mobility/CSG handling scenarios.

threeGpp.note: HeNB (Home eNodeB) detection/handling is a 3GPP-defined mobility feature; the OAM parameters for managing it as a neighbor are Nokia's own, but the underlying concept and RRC signalling are standardized.

LNHOIF.description: Configures inter-frequency handover parameters for an LTE cell, including the A3/A5 measurement event offsets, hysteresis, time-to-trigger, and report amount/interval used to trigger measurement reporting and handovers toward other LTE frequency layers. It holds many per-device-type and per-QCI variants of these thresholds (e.g. CAT-M, HPUE, QCI1) and sits under an LNCEL.
LNHOIF.officialFullName: Handover parameters to Neigbouring Interfrequency LTE Cell

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

LNHOX.description: LNHOX configures LTE handover/CSFB target parameters toward CDMA2000 1xRTT, specifying the target 1xRTT ARFCN, band class, carrier frequency, search-window size, signal-strength threshold, and the maximum number of 1xRTT CSFB targets -- used by CDMA-operator LTE deployments (e.g. legacy Verizon/Sprint networks) to redirect voice calls to the CDMA network. It belongs to the LNHOIF/LNADJX/LNHOX family of LTE inter-RAT handover objects.
LNHOX.officialFullName: Handover parameters to Neigbouring CDMA2000 1xRTT Cell

threeGpp.note: Standardized by 3GPP2 (a separate standards body for CDMA2000, not part of 3GPP), not 3GPP. CDMA2000 1xRTT/1xEV-DO air-interface parameters are specified in 3GPP2's own C.S00xx document series, entirely outside 3GPP's remit.

LNMME.description: Represents a configured MME (Mobility Management Entity) peer for the S1-MME interface of an LTE eNodeB, holding its primary IP address, name, supported PLMN list, RAT support, and current S1 link status. Multiple LNMME instances under an LNBTS define the pool of MMEs the eNodeB can connect to.

threeGpp.note: Represents an S1-MME peer; the S1AP protocol and its IEs are entirely 3GPP-defined.

LNREL.description: Represents a standard LTE-to-LTE neighbor cell relation (an ANR-managed handover relation) identified by the target cell's ECGI (PLMN, eNB ID, cell ID), with flags controlling whether handover and relation removal are allowed. It is the core object underlying both automatically discovered and manually configured neighbor relations between eNodeBs, sitting as a child of an LNCEL.

threeGpp.note: LTE-to-LTE neighbor relations are governed by the ANR management spec (TS 32.511) and configured/signalled via TS 36.331's mobility IEs.

LNRELGNBCELL.description: Defines an LTE cell's relation to a specific target 5G NR cell (identified by nrCellId and its PLMN, nrCgiPlmnId) for EN-DC dual connectivity, including whether dual connectivity to that specific NR cell is allowed (lteNrDualConnectAllowed), its current status, and whether it may be removed by SON/ANR (removeAllowed). It is a child of the LNADJGNB neighbor-gNB relation, narrowing the relation down to individual candidate NR cells.

LNRELX.description: Defines a neighbor relation from an LTE cell to an external CDMA2000 cell, paralleling LNADJX but additionally governing whether removal, CS fallback (e1xCsfbAllowed), and SRVCC handover are permitted toward that neighbor. It is used for inter-RAT mobility control between LTE and legacy CDMA2000 networks and sits under an LNCEL.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by 3GPP2 (a separate standards body for CDMA2000, not part of 3GPP), not 3GPP. CDMA2000 1xRTT/1xEV-DO air-interface parameters are specified in 3GPP2's own C.S00xx document series, entirely outside 3GPP's remit.

LNUPR.description: A cell-level profile for LTE operation in unlicensed spectrum (LTE-U/LAA, bands 46/255), covering antenna gain, band-255 measurement penalty, multiple clear-channel-assessment thresholds for data/discovery-signal transmissions, DFS (Dynamic Frequency Selection) channel offset for radar avoidance, discovery reference signal (DRS) measurement timing, LTE/Wi-Fi coexistence enablement, and maximum transmit power limits for unlicensed bands 46a/46b.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

LOGLINK.description: LOGLINK represents a logical link between two managed-object endpoints in the equipment hierarchy (e.g. between a baseband and radio module), specifying the endpoints via distinguished names and which functions the link mode carries (data, DC power). It models inter-module connectivity independent of the specific physical cable object (CABLINK).

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

LOGLINK_R.description: LOGLINK_R is the resource/state counterpart of LOGLINK, reporting the logical inter-module link's operational state in addition to its endpoint identities and carried link modes (data, DC power, synchronization).

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

LTAC.description: Defines LTE Tracking-Area-Code-specific admission control limits, such as GBR bearer limits for normal, handover, and emergency traffic and an overbooking limit, tied to a specific transport network ID. It lets an eNodeB apply different resource/admission policies per tracking area.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

LTEENB.description: Represents an external LTE eNodeB as seen from the 5G gNB side (found under the nrbts namespace), used to configure the EN-DC/X2 relationship where this gNB acts as the NR secondary node to that LTE master eNB. It records the eNodeB's ID and PLMN, its IP address and the gNB's local CU-side IP address used for the X2-C connection, and the administrative lock state and link status of that X2 connection.

threeGpp.note: LTE-NR (EN-DC) neighbor relations are governed by the multi-connectivity spec (TS 37.340), with ANR concepts from TS 32.511 also applying.

LUAC.description: Configures local user account security policy on the BTS, including account lockout duration and threshold, failed-login counting, password expiry/warning periods, and username length constraints, independent of any centralized LDAP authentication. It governs local (non-LDAP) operator login security.

LUAC_R.description: A local user-account runtime object reporting when a local (non-RADIUS/TACACS) operator account's password was last changed (localPasswdLastChangedTime), supporting security-compliance auditing of local BTS login credentials.

MFIRECEL.description: Represents cell-level radio configuration specific to MulteFire (standalone LTE-in-unlicensed-spectrum) operation, covering PRACH/PUCCH interlace allocation and reservation counts, PDSCH random-data fill behavior, transmission-opportunity retransmission counts, synchronous/asynchronous DMTC profile references, and the UE-side clear-channel-assessment threshold. It functions as the MulteFire equivalent of a standard LTE cell (LNCEL) object, configuring the specific PHY/MAC adaptations MulteFire requires for unlicensed-spectrum access.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the MulteFire Alliance (an independent industry alliance, not part of 3GPP), not 3GPP. MulteFire re-uses LTE radio technology in unlicensed spectrum without requiring a licensed anchor carrier, but is specified outside 3GPP.

MFIREPR.description: A MulteFire feature profile (MulteFire is standalone LTE operation in unlicensed spectrum without an anchor licensed carrier), configuring Listen-Before-Talk clear-channel-assessment success-rate monitoring (thresholds, hysteresis, sample counts, monitoring period), discovery reference signal timing, LTE/Wi-Fi coexistence, and non-GBR bearer thresholds for unlicensed operation.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

MFNDMTCPR.description: Configures the Discovery signals Measurement Timing Configuration (DMTC) used for neighbor-cell discovery-signal measurements in a MulteFire deployment, specifying the DMTC window length, its period, and its time offset. It allows a MulteFire cell/UE to know when and where to look for neighboring cells' discovery bursts in unlicensed spectrum.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

MNL.description: Appears to be the root 'management/non-radio-layer' container object for a broad family of site administration classes (clock, time, security, fault/performance/feature configuration, certificate handling, etc. all share its com.nokia.srbts.mnl namespace as siblings). Its own parameters cover miscellaneous site-level settings such as planned product variant, time zone, VNF IP address, and hardware-versus-plan validation.

threeGpp.note: Site-wide Nokia O&M/administrative configuration, not part of any 3GPP-defined model.

MNLENT.description: A generic sub-entity under the management/non-radio-layer branch, apparently used to configure CPRI synchronization-loss recovery behavior (break time, delay-compensation type, recovery reset delay) for a referenced target unit type. Its exact scope is inferred mainly from its parameter names rather than confirmed documentation.

MNL_R.description: MNL_R is a node-level resource/state object reporting the overall software and configuration state of a multi-technology (LTE+5G shared) BTS, including the active LTE and 5G RAT software release versions, activation timestamp, configuration-data revision number, information-model version, and which RF technologies are shared across RATs on the site. It functions as a top-level software/version-inventory record.

threeGpp.note: Site-wide Nokia O&M/administrative configuration, not part of any 3GPP-defined model.

MODPR.description: A mobility/load-balancing decision profile for an LTE cell, defining frequency-layer priority lists used for various load-balancing triggers (dedicated LTE load balancing, VoLTE handover, service-based handover, SRVCC-to-WCDMA), the percentage of UEs subject to idle-mode load balancing, inter-RAT mode behavior, carrier-aggregation blocking rules, and the target-cell selection method. It centralizes the policy inputs used by the eNodeB's mobility load-balancing algorithms.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

MOIMP.description: Configures idle-mode mobility priorities for an LTE cell, defining cell-reselection priorities and weights toward other E-UTRAN carrier frequencies (idleLBEutCelResPrio/Weight, with variants for 2/3/4 component carriers) and toward UTRAN (3G) FDD frequencies, used for idle-mode load balancing between frequency layers. It sits under the LTE cell's mobility configuration and directly influences which frequency layer idle UEs preferentially camp on.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

MOPR.description: MOPR (Mobility/Load-Balancing Operator Profile) defines operator-managed frequency-layer lists used to steer idle and connected-mode UEs across LTE and inter-RAT frequency layers for specific purposes -- CS fallback to WCDMA, dedicated VoLTE handover targets, PS handover to WCDMA, SRVCC targets, and general load-balancing candidate layers -- along with idle-mode load-balancing percentages and a target-cell-selection method, allowing fine-grained mobility/load-balancing policy per cell.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

MORED.description: MORED configures RRC connection release with redirection ('mobility redirect') behavior, controlling redirection priority and target frequency/RAT (e.g. redirecting to UTRAN), whether GSM/UTRAN system information is embedded in the redirect message, and priority handling for CS fallback and emergency calls. It supports inter-RAT mobility and CSFB procedures from an LTE cell.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

MPLANENW.description: Configures management-plane (O&M) network connectivity settings for the BTS, including the DSCP marking used for O&M traffic, the OAM peer/controller IP address, and TLS security parameters (supported versions, cipher restrictions, certificate types, renegotiation interval) protecting the management channel. It secures and prioritizes the link used for remote element management.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

MPLANENW_R.description: A runtime status object for the management-plane network's transport security, reporting whether TLS is enabled for OAM traffic (oamTlsStatus) and whether the older, less-secure TLS 1.1 protocol is still enabled (tls11EnabledStatus). It supports security-posture monitoring of the O&M channel.

MPUCCH_FDD.description: MPUCCH_FDD configures PUCCH (Physical Uplink Control Channel) resource management and RRC connection admission limits for an LTE FDD cell, including PUCCH format 1/3 resource allocation (deltaPucchShift, n1PucchAn, nPucchF3Prbs), CQI reporting resource blocks, scheduling-request period, PHICH duration, and minimum/maximum numbers of RRC connections (including reserved emergency-session capacity). It is a feature/resource configuration child of an LNCEL_FDD cell.
MPUCCH_FDD.officialFullName: Manual PUCCH Allocation Configuration for FDD Cell

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PUCCH-Config information element.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (E-UTRA); Radio Resource Control (RRC); Protocol specification

MPUCCH_TDD.description: Configures the manual/static PUCCH resource allocation for a TDD LTE cell - fixed sizes for CQI, ACK/NACK, and format-3 PUCCH resources, PHICH duration/resources, and maximum/minimum RRC connection counts - serving as the counterpart to the adaptive APUCCH_TDD configuration. It defines the baseline fixed PUCCH capacity plan for the cell.
MPUCCH_TDD.officialFullName: Manual PUCCH Allocation Configuration for TDD Cell

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PUCCH-Config information element.
