MRBTS.description: The root managed object representing the entire physical BTS/gNB site, under which all other equipment and logical function objects (EQM, LNBTS, NRBTS, etc.) are nested. Its parameters cover the site's identity and physical location, such as BTS name, latitude/longitude/altitude, and overall blocking state.

threeGpp.note: Corresponds to the generic NRM's top-level ManagedElement IOC; the granular equipment hierarchy underneath it (cabinets/modules/etc.) is Nokia's own extension beyond what 3GPP's generic model specifies.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Generic Network Resource Model (NRM) Integration Reference Point (IRP); Information Service (IS)

MRBTSDESC.description: MRBTSDESC holds descriptive metadata about the MRBTS site object, including a human-readable descriptive name, integration/commissioning information, the MRBTS configuration type, and target-parameter information used during commissioning. It is a small companion object to the MRBTS root, carrying site-identification and integration bookkeeping rather than radio/equipment configuration.

threeGpp.note: Free-text/descriptive metadata about the site -- not part of the 3GPP NRM's attribute set.

MTRACE.description: Configures cell-level subscriber and radio tracing (call/measurement trace, similar in scope to CTRLTS but at the cell rather than BTS level), including EUTRAN trace ID and its PLMN components, per-cell trace mode and maximum concurrently traced UEs/MDT UEs, angle-of-arrival tracing, PCMD (Per Call Measurement Data) and UE-throughput measurement-report activation, and MDT anonymization behavior. It supports network optimization, troubleshooting, and regulatory/measurement tracing at the individual cell level.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

NBIOTPR.description: A large feature-configuration profile for NB-IoT (Narrowband Internet of Things), covering HARQ ACK/NACK repetition counts per coverage class (CE Level 0/1/2) for Msg4, coverage-enhancement search-space profiles for extended/normal/robust coverage, default paging cycle and number of paging repetitions, initial MCS for DL/UL, and repetition counts for NPDCCH random access, NPDSCH, and NPUSCH. It fully parameterizes how the cell serves NB-IoT devices across different coverage conditions.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

NECERT_R.description: Represents an installed X.509 certificate on the network element, exposing standard certificate fields such as issuer and subject (issuedTo/issuer), serial number, signature algorithm, key usage, subject alternate name, key identifiers, trust chain, and validity period (validFrom/validTo). It is used to inventory and monitor the certificates the BTS uses for IPsec, TLS/OAM, or 802.1X security.

NOTE.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "NOTE". It did not appear in the researched sample set. Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

NOTES.description: A free-text annotation object used to attach operator comments or documentation notes to the BTS configuration for record-keeping purposes. It carries no functional radio, transport, or hardware parameters — it exists purely to hold human-readable notes within the configuration file.

threeGpp.note: Site-wide Nokia O&M/administrative configuration, not part of any 3GPP-defined model.

NRBEAMMAP.description: Defines the mapping between logical beam identifiers and the physical antenna beam patterns (azimuth/elevation weights) used by the Active Antenna System for NR SSB/CSI-RS beamforming and beam sweeping on this cell.

threeGpp.note: Beam management procedures themselves are standardized (TS 38.213/38.214), but this specific logical-beam-ID-to-physical-antenna-pattern mapping table is Nokia's own implementation detail, not a 3GPP-defined structure.

NRBTS.description: NRBTS is the top-level logical 5G gNB object (the NR counterpart to LNBTS), sitting under the MRBTS site root and representing the entire gNB's identity and node-wide configuration. With over 500 parameters it primarily consists of feature-activation toggles (3GPP release features, RTPM performance monitoring, TCP MSS clamping, QoS-flow handling, mobility and load-control behaviors) that apply across all NR cells and DUs hosted by this gNB.

threeGpp.note: Aggregates the 5G NRM's GNBCUCPFunction/GNBDUFunction concepts under one site-level object.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G Network Resource Model (NRM); Stage 2 and stage 3

NRCBRSPR.description: An NR CBRS profile object holding the Priority Access License (PAL) / General Authorized Access (GAA) channel and priority configuration a cell uses when operating in the shared CBRS band, referenced by cells that need CBRS-specific spectrum-sharing behavior.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

NRCBSD.description: Represents this base station's identity/registration as a CBSD (Citizens Broadband Radio Service Device) for operation in the US CBRS band (3.55-3.7 GHz, NR band n48). Holds the FCC ID, serial number, and registration data the SAS (Spectrum Access System) uses to authorize and manage the device's spectrum grants.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

NRCBSDCELL.description: Links an NR cell to its CBSD (Citizens Broadband Radio Service Device) registration and the specific SAS-granted CBRS channel/frequency it is authorized to transmit on, tying the logical cell to its CBRS spectrum grant.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

NRCELL.description: NRCELL is the core 5G NR cell managed object, representing a single NR cell's full radio configuration. Its very large parameter set (500+) covers mobility measurement events (A1/A2/etc. thresholds for both SA and NSA/EN-DC modes, and voice-over-NR specific variants), among many other cell-level radio parameters. It is the NR analog of LNCEL and sits under an NRBTS/NRDU in the site hierarchy.

threeGpp.note: The class corresponds to the 5G NRM's NRCellDU/NRCellCU IOCs (TS 28.541); most of its RRC-facing parameters are themselves specified in TS 38.331.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G Network Resource Model (NRM); Stage 2 and stage 3
NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRCELLGRP.description: NRCELLGRP configures a group of NR cells that share scheduling and resource-management behavior, covering scheduler load/HARQ tuning (maxDlHarqTx, forgetting ratios per frequency range), CSI reporting periodicity and load-based adjustment, beamforming grid selection, PUCCH beam constraints for FR2 (mmWave), and handover admission counts. It groups related NRCELL instances (e.g. cells sharing a baseband/carrier resource pool) under an NRDU.

threeGpp.note: A cell-grouping construct within the 5G NRM's cell hierarchy.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G Network Resource Model (NRM); Stage 2 and stage 3

NRCELL_FDD.description: Represents a 5G NR cell configured for FDD (Frequency Division Duplex) operation, as distinct from the more common TDD NR cell, with separate downlink and uplink NR-ARFCN center frequencies (nrarfcnDl/nrarfcnUl) and channel bandwidths (chBwDl/chBwUl), asymmetric-bandwidth guard-band handling, and O-RAN fronthaul activation (actOran). It sits under an NR DU/gNB in the site hierarchy, functioning as the FDD counterpart to the standard NRCELL object.

threeGpp.note: The class corresponds to the 5G NRM's NRCellDU/NRCellCU IOCs (TS 28.541); most of its RRC-facing parameters are themselves specified in TS 38.331.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G Network Resource Model (NRM); Stage 2 and stage 3
NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRCUUP.description: NRCUUP represents the gNB-CU-UP (Centralized Unit, User-Plane) function in a disaggregated gNB architecture, identified by its own gNB-CU-UP ID and holding the local and remote IP addresses used for the E1 interface (and user-plane transport) between the CU control-plane and user-plane functions. It models the split-gNB architecture alongside NRDU (the DU function).

threeGpp.note: Corresponds to the 5G NRM's GNBCUUPFunction IOC.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G Network Resource Model (NRM); Stage 2 and stage 3

NRDCDPR.description: A dual-connectivity (EN-DC) profile controlling how an LTE cell manages adding and maintaining an NR secondary cell group, including power-headroom-reporting timers (tPeriodicPhr/tProhibitPhr), maximum power offsets allotted to the LTE (MCG) and NR (SCG) legs (enDCpMaxEUTRApowerOffset/enDCpMaxNRpowerOffset), the pathloss-change trigger for B1 measurement (dlPathlossChg/bufTrigForB1Nr), and bearer-context-list sorting behavior. It is a feature-configuration object rather than a physical/radio object.
NRDCDPR.officialFullName: New Radio Dual Connectivity Default Profile

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

NRDRB.description: NRDRB represents the Data Radio Bearer (DRB) configuration for a 5G NR cell/DU, defining bearer-level behavior such as PDCP status reporting on resume, discard timers, dual-connectivity (X2/Xx) transmission coordination between the master and secondary node, and downlink data-split buffering thresholds for split bearers. It is a child configuration object under an NR cell or gNB-DU that governs how user-plane data bearers are handled across the split RLC/PDCP/MAC layers described by its sibling objects (NRDRB_PDCP, NRDRB_MAC, NRDRB_RLC_AM).

NRDRB_5QI.description: Maps one or more 5QI (5G QoS Identifier) values to a Data Radio Bearer configuration for NR and indicates whether data forwarding is used for that DRB (e.g. during handover), controlling how NR QoS flows are grouped onto radio bearers with consistent scheduling and treatment.

threeGpp.note: The 5QI (5G QoS Identifier) standardized characteristics table is defined in this spec, §5.7.4.

specs.title: System architecture for the 5G System (5GS)

NRDRB_MAC.description: NRDRB_MAC configures MAC-layer scheduling behavior for a 5G NR Data Radio Bearer's logical channel, including the logical channel group ID (lcgid), prioritized bit rate, scheduling priority, and delay target used by the gNB scheduler for QoS-aware resource allocation. It is a child object of NRDRB, alongside NRDRB_PDCP and NRDRB_RLC_AM, together modeling the full NR user-plane protocol stack per bearer.

NRDRB_PDCP.description: NRDRB_PDCP configures the PDCP (Packet Data Convergence Protocol) sublayer behavior for a 5G NR Data Radio Bearer, including reordering timers (tReorderingDl/Ul), buffer discard thresholds, header-compression context limits (maxCidAllowed), and CU flow-control profile selection used in split CU/DU deployments. It is a child object of NRDRB and directly implements 3GPP PDCP-layer parameters for the bearer.

NRDRB_RLC_AM.description: NRDRB_RLC_AM configures RLC Acknowledged Mode (AM) behavior for a 5G NR Data Radio Bearer, including ARQ retransmission thresholds, poll timers/counters (dlTPollRetr, dlPollByte/PDU), reassembly timers, and the DU-side flow-control profile. It is a child of NRDRB and implements the 3GPP RLC-AM sublayer for bearers requiring reliable delivery.

NRDRB_RLC_UM.description: Configures RLC (Radio Link Control) parameters for a 5G NR Data Radio Bearer operating in Unacknowledged Mode (UM), including the UM sequence-number length and the DL/UL reassembly timers used to reorder and discard RLC UM PDUs. It is a child configuration object of an NR cell/bearer profile, used for delay-sensitive traffic (e.g., voice) that does not require RLC retransmission.

NRDRX.description: Defines a Discontinuous Reception (DRX) profile for a 5G NR cell, specifying the DRX long cycle, on-duration timer, inactivity timer, and HARQ RTT/retransmission timers for both uplink and downlink, used to let connected UEs periodically power down their receiver to conserve battery. It is the NR counterpart to the LTE DRX/SDRX objects.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

NRDU.description: NRDU represents the gNB-DU (Distributed Unit) function of a split gNB, identified by its gNB-DU ID/name and RRC version, holding the local CU IP address used for the F1 interface. It also carries carrier-aggregation feature toggles (inter-gNB CA, non-beamformed/beamformed CA mixing, CA with 3 transmit paths) and administrative state, and typically hosts one or more NRCELL/NRCELLGRP instances beneath it.

threeGpp.note: Corresponds to the 5G NRM's GNBDUFunction IOC.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G Network Resource Model (NRM); Stage 2 and stage 3

NRIAFIM.description: NRIAFIM configures intra-frequency idle-mode mobility parameters for NR, including the minimum required RX level for cell reselection (qRxLevMin), intra-frequency search thresholds (sIntraSearchP/Q), the cell-reselection timer (tReselectionNr), and the number of transmitted SSBs used for measurement averaging. It governs how idle UEs reselect between NR cells on the same frequency.

threeGpp.note: NR idle-mode mobility and Tracking Area configuration are broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRIRFIM.description: NR equivalent of the LTE IRFIM object: holds Inter-RAT / Inter-Frequency idle-mode mobility parameters (cell reselection priorities, thresholds, and related tuning) that control how idle-mode UEs move between this NR frequency layer and other NR or LTE frequency layers.

threeGpp.note: NR idle-mode mobility and Tracking Area configuration are broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRMEASDPR.description: NRMEASDPR ('NR measurement/dual-connectivity profile') defines LTE-to-NR measurement configuration used for EN-DC (dual connectivity) NR secondary-node addition, including RSRP/RSRQ filter coefficients (separate for the measured serving vs. NR reference signal), whether measurement gaps are enabled for NR measurements, quantity-config selection, and B1-event retry/supervision timers. It is configured on the LTE anchor cell to control when/how the UE measures and reports NR cells for EN-DC.

threeGpp.note: NR idle-mode mobility and Tracking Area configuration are broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRPLMN.description: Defines a Public Land Mobile Network identity (MCC/MNC with MNC length) broadcast or supported by an NR cell/gNB, analogous to the LTE PLMN list object but in the NR namespace. Multiple instances allow a shared or multi-operator gNB to advertise several PLMNs.

threeGpp.note: Broadcast PLMN identity is carried in SIB1's PLMN-IdentityInfoList, a 3GPP-defined RRC structure.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRPLMN_SUPPORT.description: Declares a Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN, via mcc/mnc) that an NR cell or gNB supports, together with the associated network slice identifiers (S-NSSAI, expressed via sst and the AMF list snssaiAMFList/snssaiAMFNumber) usable by that PLMN. It links the 5G radio access network's broadcast PLMN/slice support to the 5G core's AMF pool, and typically sits under an NR cell or gNB's core-network-facing configuration.

threeGpp.note: Per-PLMN NG-RAN support/broadcast is signalled via NGAP and SIB1.

specs.title: NG-RAN; NG Application Protocol (NGAP)

NRPMCCP.description: NRPMCCP is a performance-monitoring control object that enables specific NR counter categories -- historical measurement-report statistics, uplink RIP (Received Interference Power) counters, radio quality measurement counts, tracking-area counters, and throughput distribution updates -- governing which NR performance counters are actively collected.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of NR/5GC performance measurements in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G performance measurements

NRPMRNL.description: NRPMRNL is a performance-monitoring configuration object that enables/controls a very large set of NR 'Radio Network Layer' measurement indicator counters (beamforming, carrier aggregation, cell availability, cell-group measurements, and many others prefixed 'miNr...'). It does not represent physical or radio configuration itself but rather which NR PM counter families are collected for reporting.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of NR/5GC performance measurements in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected.

specs.title: Management and orchestration; 5G performance measurements

NRRFSP_PROFILE.description: NRRFSP_PROFILE defines an RFSP (RAT/Frequency Selection Priority) index profile for 5G NR -- a subscriber-group priority value, normally supplied by the core network (AMF/HSS), that the gNB uses to bias idle-mode camping and inter-frequency/inter-RAT redirection decisions for that subscriber group.

threeGpp.note: RFSP Index and Subscriber Profile ID (SPID) are standardized Information Elements carried over S1AP (also referenced from the core network side in TS 23.401's Annex on RAT/Frequency Selection Priority).

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN); S1 Application Protocol (S1AP)

NRSASUSERGROUP.description: Holds Spectrum Access System (SAS) user/group credential and grouping information for CBRS operation -- the operator/user account details the SAS uses to authenticate spectrum grant requests for this site's CBSDs.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

NRSCTP.description: NRSCTP configures an SCTP association profile used for NG-interface signaling transport between the gNB and the 5G core (AMF), tuning parameters such as heartbeat interval, retransmission counts/timeouts (RTO min/initial/max), max burst, SACK delay, and payload size. It is the NR/5G counterpart to LTE's SCTP association object, supporting the NGAP signaling protocol.

threeGpp.note: SCTP is itself an IETF protocol (RFC 4960), but 3GPP specifies its use as the NG-interface signalling transport in this spec.

specs.title: NG-RAN; NG signalling transport

NRSPID_PROFILE.description: NRSPID_PROFILE defines an SPID (Subscriber Profile ID for RAT/Frequency Priority) value for NR, analogous to the RFSP profile, used to apply subscriber-group-specific camping and mobility priorities across frequency layers/RATs.

threeGpp.note: RFSP Index and Subscriber Profile ID (SPID) are standardized Information Elements carried over S1AP (also referenced from the core network side in TS 23.401's Annex on RAT/Frequency Selection Priority).

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN); S1 Application Protocol (S1AP)

NRSYSINFO_PROFILE.description: NRSYSINFO_PROFILE defines System Information Block (SIB) broadcast configuration for an NR cell per 3GPP TS 38.331 -- SIB scheduling list, periodicity, broadcast status, and scope -- together with idle/inactive-mode cell-reselection relaxation parameters (measurement relaxation hysteresis for high/medium mobility states, cell-change-count thresholds, Qhyst) that reduce UE measurement activity for stationary or low-mobility devices.

threeGpp.note: NR System Information Blocks and their content are 3GPP-defined broadcast structures.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

NRX2LINK_TRUST.description: Defines a trusted X2 peer for NR/EN-DC purposes, specifying the IPv4 address of a trusted peer node (ipV4Addr) and a trust-control setting (x2LinkTrustCtrl) that governs whether X2 signaling from that address is accepted. It is a security/access-control object protecting the gNB's X2-C interface from untrusted peers.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP requires inter-node interfaces to be secured (see the Network Domain Security annex); this specific trusted-peer list mechanism is Nokia's own implementation.

specs.title: Security architecture and procedures for 5G system

NTP.description: NTP configures the Network Time Protocol client used by the BTS/gNB for coarse time synchronization, including the list of NTP server IP addresses/FQDNs, DSCP marking for NTP traffic, maximum tolerated time error, alarming threshold, and UTC-GPS leap-second offset handling. It is a synchronization support object that complements GNSS/PTP-based sync sources.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IETF (RFC 5905, NTPv4), not 3GPP. Coarse time sync, unrelated to 3GPP.

NTPS.description: Configures NTP-based synchronization on the older Flexi Zone LTE product line, listing the NTP servers to sync against (ntpSyncServers), the local IP address mapping used to reach them (ntpSyncLocalIpMapping), and how frequently the client polls them (ntpSyncPollingRate). It is functionally equivalent to the AirScale NTP client configuration (NTP_R).

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IETF (RFC 5905, NTPv4), not 3GPP. Coarse time sync, unrelated to 3GPP.

NTP_R.description: A runtime status object for the Network Time Protocol client, listing the configured NTP server address(es), each server's per-server sync status, the stratum number of the reference clock, and the overall NTP synchronization status. It reflects the live state of time synchronization used for O&M/logging timestamps and possibly a coarse frequency reference.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IETF (RFC 5905, NTPv4), not 3GPP. Coarse time sync, unrelated to 3GPP.

PCP2QMAP.description: Defines a mapping from Ethernet 802.1p Priority Code Point (PCP) values (0-7) to internal hardware transmit queues, analogous to DSCPTOQMAP but keyed on the VLAN tag's priority bits rather than the IP DSCP field. It is used by the transport network layer's QoS scheduler to prioritize Layer-2-tagged traffic.

threeGpp.note: Transport-layer QoS marking (DiffServ/DSCP is IETF RFC 2474; 802.1p/PCP is IEEE 802.1Q) -- 3GPP doesn't standardize a vendor's specific DSCP-to-queue mapping table.

PDCCH.description: PDCCH configures Physical Downlink Control Channel behavior for an NR cell, specifically the aggregation-level (AL) selection strategy for different DCI (Downlink Control Information) message types -- dedicated scheduling, paging, random-access completion/Msg2, and system information -- along with proactive/reactive downgrade rules between AL16 and AL8 to manage control-channel capacity.

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PDCCH-Config / PDCCH-ConfigCommon information elements.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

PDCCH_CONFIG_COMMON.description: PDCCH_CONFIG_COMMON defines the common (cell-wide) PDCCH search-space and CORESET configuration for an NR cell per 3GPP TS 38.331 -- including CORESET ID, DCI format, monitoring symbol/slot offset, periodicity, search-space type (common vs. UE-specific), and the number of PDCCH candidates configured per aggregation level. It complements PDCCH's aggregation-level selection logic with the standardized control-resource-set definition.

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PDCCH-Config / PDCCH-ConfigCommon information elements.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

PDCCH_CONFIG_DEDICATED.description: Defines the UE-specific (dedicated) PDCCH (Physical Downlink Control Channel) configuration for a 5G NR cell, including the CORESET (Control Resource Set) definition, CCE-to-REG mapping, interleaver and REG bundle sizes, DCI format, monitoring periodicity/offset, and the number of PDCCH candidates configured per aggregation level (AL1/2/4/8/16). This is a standard 3GPP NR physical-layer control-channel configuration object nested under an NR cell/BWP.

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PDCCH-Config / PDCCH-ConfigCommon information elements.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

PDSCH.description: PDSCH represents Physical Downlink Shared Channel configuration for a 5G NR cell, the standard 3GPP downlink data channel used to carry user-plane and some control data. The observed parameter (pdschRat0RbgConfig) configures resource-block-group sizing for PDSCH scheduling. It sits as a child configuration object under an NR cell/DU.

threeGpp.note: Configures the RRC PDSCH-Config information element.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

PFOE_R.description: A runtime equipment-status object in the equipment-runtime (eqmr) namespace; no sample parameters were captured in this dataset. Based on its naming pattern (similar to POE) and placement alongside other hardware runtime-mirror classes, it most likely reports Power-over-Ethernet feed/output status for a hardware port, but this is a low-confidence inference.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

PKTFLTR.description: Represents an IP packet filter rule object, typically referenced by or associated with the FIREWALL class, used to define match criteria (source/destination address, port, protocol) for permitting or blocking specific traffic flows at the BTS's transport network layer. No sample parameters were captured, but it functions as a security/traffic-filtering building block.

PLMN.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "PLMN". It did not appear in the researched sample set. Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

PMCADM.description: The site-wide Performance Management Configuration Administration object, setting the PM reporting interval and the destination IP/file-count limits used when uploading performance measurement files. It governs how and where the BTS exports its counter and KPI data.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of E-UTRAN performance counters in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected, so applies loosely -- see the note before assuming every counter this config touches has a matching 3GPP counter definition.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Performance Management (PM); Performance measurements Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN)

PMCADM_R.description: A performance-management collection/administration runtime object under the site management-network-layer branch. No sample parameters were captured in this dataset, so its precise scope is inferred generically as controlling or reporting on PM (performance measurement) data-collection administration for the node.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of E-UTRAN performance counters in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected, so applies loosely -- see the note before assuming every counter this config touches has a matching 3GPP counter definition.

PMCCP.description: A small performance-management configuration object defining thresholds used to trigger enhanced or fast reporting, such as a fast RRC-connection-setup-request threshold and a PRB (Physical Resource Block) utilization threshold. It supports proactive congestion and quality monitoring.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of E-UTRAN performance counters in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected, so applies loosely -- see the note before assuming every counter this config touches has a matching 3GPP counter definition.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Performance Management (PM); Performance measurements Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN)

PMMNL.description: A performance-monitoring/statistics configuration object in the site management-network-layer (mnl) branch, controlling collection intervals and enabling of measurement counters related to synchronization and fronthaul quality: GNSS antenna speed and time-error stats, PTP/eCPRI master statistics, O-RAN radio-unit/transport statistics, and SyncE network-rearrangement counts. It configures which sync/fronthaul-related PM counters the BTS collects and how often.
PMMNL.officialFullName: Performance Management Administration for Management Layer

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of E-UTRAN performance counters in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected, so applies loosely -- see the note before assuming every counter this config touches has a matching 3GPP counter definition.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Performance Management (PM); Performance measurements Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN)

PMPLM.description: A performance-management configuration object defining a set of graduated cell/uplane-load threshold bins (0a-0e) and tracking how often each load level occurs, used to bucket and report load distribution over time for capacity monitoring.

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of E-UTRAN performance counters in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected, so applies loosely -- see the note before assuming every counter this config touches has a matching 3GPP counter definition.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Performance Management (PM); Performance measurements Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN)

PMQAP.description: Defines a QoS-aware performance measurement profile that segments PM counters by dimensions such as ARP range, QCI range, UE category, and PLMN, letting operators collect KPIs broken down by service or QoS class rather than only in aggregate.
PMQAP.officialFullName: Performance Monitoring QCI and ARP Profiles identifier

threeGpp.note: 3GPP defines a standardized catalog of E-UTRAN performance counters in this spec; this object controls which of Nokia's (standardized-and-proprietary) counters get collected, so applies loosely -- see the note before assuming every counter this config touches has a matching 3GPP counter definition.

specs.title: Telecommunication management; Performance Management (PM); Performance measurements Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN)

PMRNL.description: A performance-management configuration object that enables or disables specific measurement-type ('mt*') counter groups covering a broad range of areas - baseband pooling, carrier-aggregation relations, cell availability/load/throughput, and CAT-M accessibility/mobility/retainability KPIs. It controls which PM statistics categories are actively collected and reported.
PMRNL.officialFullName: PM counters configuration for radio network layer

It supports RF/mobility performance analysis by shaping how measurement-report statistics are bucketed and stored.

It does not represent physical hardware but rather controls which transport PM counter groups are active and how often they are sampled, typically as a site-level configuration object.

It is a performance-monitoring configuration object in the transport (tnl) domain.

PNASC.description: PNASC configures port-based network access control (IEEE 802.1X) on an Ethernet port, including a guard timer for the EAP authentication exchange and a destination group for unauthenticated/authenticated traffic, used to restrict network access on the BTS's transport ports until a device or link is authenticated.
PNASC.officialFullName: Port Network Access Security for FZM

threeGpp.note: Standardized by IEEE (802.1X), not 3GPP. Port-based network access control is an IEEE Ethernet standard, unrelated to 3GPP.

POE.description: Enables or disables Power-over-Ethernet feed (actPowerPoE) on a given Ethernet port of the BTS, used to power an externally connected device (such as a small radio unit, media converter, or access point) directly over the data cable. It is a transport/hardware-adjacent networking object in the Flexi Zone product line.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IEEE (802.3af/at/bt), not 3GPP. Power-over-Ethernet, unrelated to 3GPP.

POWERGROUP_R.description: A runtime status object representing a power supply/power-distribution group within the BTS cabinet, exposing its operationalState. It groups one or more power feeds or power modules that supply DC power to baseband, radio, or auxiliary equipment, and is reported under the equipment management hardware tree.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

PREEMPPR.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "PREEMPPR". It did not appear in the researched sample set. Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

PTPMASTER.description: Configures the BTS to act as an IEEE 1588 PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master/grandmaster clock, specifying the PTP domain number, multicast MAC address used for PTP messages, BMCA priority (priority2), the applicable PTP profile (standardProfile, e.g. G.8275.1), the phase-holdover alarm threshold, and the physical port used to transmit PTP master messages (ptpMasterPortDN). It allows the node to distribute precise time/phase to downstream nodes rather than only consuming it.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8271/G.8275 Telecom Profiles) and IEEE (1588 PTP), not 3GPP. 3GPP requires certain synchronization ACCURACY budgets for radio operation (e.g. TS 36.133/38.133), but does not itself define the PTP/eCPRI synchronization protocol used to achieve them.

QOS.description: Defines QoS marking and mapping rules for transport traffic, mapping DSCP values and traffic types to per-hop-behavior classes (assured-forwarding classes, best-effort, VLAN priority) and enabling per-hop-behavior counters. It governs how outgoing IP packets from the BTS are prioritized across the backhaul network.

threeGpp.note: Transport-layer QoS marking (DiffServ/DSCP is IETF RFC 2474; 802.1p/PCP is IEEE 802.1Q) -- 3GPP doesn't standardize a vendor's specific DSCP-to-queue mapping table.

REDRT.description: Configures RRC connection release redirection targets and priorities for an LTE cell, controlling which inter-RAT frequency/band (CDMA, UTRAN, GERAN) a UE is redirected to, for example during CS fallback or emergency calls, and whether target-RAT system information is piggy-backed in the redirect message. It sits under an LNCEL and is central to CSFB and inter-RAT redirection behavior.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

RETU.description: RETU represents a RET (Remote Electrical Tilt) actuator unit that mechanically controls the downtilt angle of one or more antenna sub-units. Parameters define the current/min/max electrical tilt angle, mechanical tilt offset, the sector it serves, and the list of antenna line devices (ANTL) it is associated with. It sits under the equipment hierarchy, connected via the antenna line to the associated RF module.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

RETU_R.description: RETU_R is the resource/state counterpart of RETU, reporting the RET actuator's availability, operational, and procedural status in addition to the same tilt-angle and antenna-line-association parameters, reflecting the real-time state of the antenna tilt hardware.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

RFREQ.description: The exact purpose of this class could not be confidently determined; no sample parameters were captured for this dataset. Given the abbreviation and its placement under the site management-network-layer (mnl) namespace, it may relate to a radio- or reference-frequency management setting, but this is a low-confidence, largely speculative interpretation.

RFRES.description: RFRES stores the results of an RF test or calibration procedure run on the radio/antenna hardware (e.g. a forward/reverse power or return-loss test), recording the actual start/stop time, forward and reverse test dispositions, overall test outcome, and any additional outcome details. It is likely produced by running a test defined via the TEST object.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

RFTHLD.description: RFTHLD defines alarm threshold levels for RF hardware health metrics on a radio module -- power error (high/low), operating temperature (high/low), receive antenna RSSI and RTWP (Received Total Wideband Power), and transmit antenna VSWR (Voltage Standing Wave Ratio, indicating antenna/feeder faults) -- used to raise equipment alarms when RF hardware readings exceed acceptable bounds.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

RIBS.description: RIBS appears to reference a specific 'source' LTE cell by its EARFCN and cell ID, suggesting it supports a coordination or interference-management feature (for example, identifying a nearby/interfering cell that a mitigation or coexistence scheme should account for). Its exact purpose could not be determined with confidence from the available parameters alone.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

RIBS_R.description: A runtime status object in the site management-network-layer (mnl) branch reporting a synchronization status (ribsSyncStatus) between some internal information base and its replica, most likely related to configuration or routing-table synchronization between redundant control units. The precise scope of 'RIBS' could not be determined with confidence from the available parameters.

threeGpp.note: Site-wide Nokia O&M/administrative configuration, not part of any 3GPP-defined model.

RIM.description: Configures RAN Information Management (RIM) procedure parameters used by the eNodeB to exchange system-information and load-related messages with GERAN/UTRAN nodes over the core network, primarily to support Circuit-Switched Fallback (CSFB) — including keep-alive, polling, and RIM-info-request timers for GERAN (G) and UTRAN (U), maximum system-information sizes under good/weak radio conditions, and the radio-condition threshold used to decide CSFB behavior. RIM is a standard 3GPP inter-RAT signaling mechanism.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

RMOD.description: Represents a Radio Module — a Remote Radio Head (RRH) or Active Antenna System unit performing RF transmission/reception and digital baseband-to-RF conversion. Its parameters cover administrative state, PIM cancellation, energy-saving mode, CPRI/RF sharing, digital combining mode, and management IP protocol version, and it sits under a CABINET/APEQM branch, connected to a BBMOD via a CABLINK.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

RMOD_R.description: The runtime/inventory counterpart to the RMOD configuration object, reporting a radio module's live operational status - administrative/availability state, active software build/version, chassis serial number, and the list of LTE/NR cells currently active on it. It reflects actual detected hardware and service state rather than planned configuration.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

RNC.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "RNC". It did not appear in the researched sample set. Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

RSL.description: RSL configures a physical serial control/signaling link -- likely the AISG/RS-485-style link that carries DC phantom power and HDLC-framed control data between a radio/baseband module and its connected antenna line devices (RET motors, TMAs) -- via the dcVoltageEnabled and hdlcCommunicationAllowed flags. It sits in the equipment (eqm) hierarchy alongside ALD/ANTL-related objects.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

RSL_R.description: RSL_R is the resource/state counterpart of RSL, reporting administrative/operational/availability/usage status for the antenna-line control/signaling link (DC voltage and HDLC communication settings) in addition to its configuration parameters.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by AISG (Antenna Interface Standards Group), not 3GPP. Remote Electrical Tilt / Tower-Mounted Amplifier control protocol (AISG v2/v3), an industry standard independent of 3GPP.

RTPOL.description: Defines a policy-based routing rule for the transport network, matching traffic by source IP address/prefix and directing it to a specific routing table (via routingTableDN/Ptr) with a defined evaluation order, letting the BTS route different traffic classes over different paths.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

SASUSERGROUP.description: Defines a CBRS SAS (Spectrum Access System) user/CBSD group identifier used when registering the BTS's CBRS-band radios with a Spectrum Access System, allowing multiple CBSDs (e.g., co-located sectors) to be grouped under one operator/deployment for coordinated spectrum grants. No sample parameters were captured, but it functions alongside CBRSPR in CBRS deployments.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the Wireless Innovation Forum (WInnForum) and US FCC Part 96 rules, not 3GPP. Citizens Broadband Radio Service (band 48, US 3.5 GHz shared spectrum) is a US regulatory/WInnForum framework, not a 3GPP specification (though the radio cell itself, once configured, operates per normal 3GPP band definitions).

SCTP.description: Configures an SCTP association's transport-layer reliability parameters (retransmission counts, RTO min/max, heartbeat interval, SACK delay/frequency, and setup retry timing for S1/X2/M3 interfaces). SCTP is the transport protocol underlying LTE control-plane signaling (S1-MME, X2, M3), and this object tunes its resilience characteristics.

threeGpp.note: SCTP is itself an IETF protocol (RFC 4960), but 3GPP specifies its use as the S1-interface signalling transport in this spec.

specs.title: Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access Network (E-UTRAN); S1 signalling transport

SDRX.description: Defines a 'smart' DRX profile that extends standard DRX with an additional short-cycle stage and inactivity-factor-based switching logic, letting the eNodeB adapt UE sleep cycles more aggressively for battery savings while limiting latency impact. It is referenced by cells or QCI-based profiles that enable smart DRX behavior.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

SECADM.description: The site-wide Security Administration object, configuring platform security policy such as SSH service accounts, service-port hardening, password/certificate strength rules (minimum RSA key length, disallowing weak SHA-1 chains), login banners, and web UI session timeouts. It centralizes security hardening settings for the BTS.

SECADM_R.description: A security-administration runtime status object reporting the current state of node-security hardening settings, specifically whether SSH access is enabled for service accounts (serviceAccountSshStatus) and the open/closed status of various service ports (servicePortStatus). It supports security-compliance monitoring on the BTS's management plane.

SECPRM.description: SECPRM holds general security-related O&M parameters for the BTS, such as the login banner text shown to users on management interfaces and the idle session timeout for local craft/terminal access. It is a site-level security configuration object in the Flexi Zone (NOKLTE) product line.

SERVEDAMF.description: SERVEDAMF configures an AMF (Access and Mobility Management Function) instance served by the gNB over the NG interface, holding the AMF's IP address, name, region/set/pointer identifiers that together form its GUAMI, PLMN identity (MCC/MNC), default-AMF flag, and NG link status. It is the 5G-core-facing counterpart to LTE's served-MME configuration.

threeGpp.note: AMF configuration/selection information is carried over NGAP.

specs.title: NG-RAN; NG Application Protocol (NGAP)

SFP.description: Represents a physical SFP/SFP+ pluggable optical or electrical transceiver module inserted into an Ethernet or CPRI/eCPRI port of the BTS, identified by the hardware port it occupies (hwPortId). It is an equipment inventory object under the equipment (EQM) hardware branch.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

SFP_R.description: SFP_R is the resource/state object for a pluggable optical/electrical transceiver (SFP/SFP+) installed in a network port, reporting administrative/operational/availability status, connector and compliance codes, manufacture date code, and -- for tunable DWDM optics -- the tuning method, channel range, grid spacing, and currently tuned channel/frequency. It sits under the equipment (eqmr) hierarchy, typically as a child of an Ethernet port or link object.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

SIB.description: Configures the content of System Information Blocks broadcast by an LTE cell, including access-class-barring parameters for specific services (MMTEL voice/video, SMS) and their associated barring timers and factors. It directly controls what UEs read from broadcast signaling before and during RRC connection establishment, and sits under an LNCEL.

threeGpp.note: System Information Blocks and their content are entirely 3GPP-defined broadcast structures.

SLCELLDRCONF.description: Configures the 'sleeping cell' detection-and-recovery self-healing feature, capping the maximum number of automatic recovery actions allowed per day at different granularities: per baseband unit (Bbu), per BTS, per cell, and per RF module (Rfm). It is a SON/self-healing feature-configuration object under the site management-network-layer branch, preventing automated recovery actions from looping excessively.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

SMOD.description: Represents a System Module - a control or auxiliary hardware module within a cabinet responsible for functions such as clock distribution, climate control, and port management. Parameters cover its physical position in the subrack, operating/port mode, climate-control profiling, and planned product code, and it is the parent of the CLOCK object.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

SMOD_R.description: SMOD_R is the resource/state object for a System Module (a core baseband/control board), reporting its administrative/operational/procedural/usage state, physical slot position, hardware inventory identifiers (product code, serial number, core HW board identifiers), and which radio access technologies (EUTRA/LTE, UTRAN/3G, GERAN/2G) it can support in a shared/multi-RAT deployment.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

SNSSAI.description: SNSSAI represents an S-NSSAI (Single Network Slice Selection Assistance Information), the 3GPP identifier for a 5G network slice, defined by its Slice/Service Type (sst) and associated PLMN(s). The gNB broadcasts and applies this object to support network-slice-aware cell access and admission control for 5G core network slicing.

threeGpp.note: S-NSSAI (network slice identity) is defined in the 5G System Architecture spec (also numbered in TS 23.003).

specs.title: System architecture for the 5G System (5GS)

STPG.description: STPG (synchronization timing priority group) defines a prioritized list of synchronization sources (e.g. SyncE, external 2.048MHz reference, 1PPS/ToD via fronthaul) with per-source priority, SSM (Synchronization Status Message) usage and quality thresholds, and clock protocol selection, used by the clock subsystem to automatically select the best available timing reference.

SYNC.description: The site's overall synchronization configuration object, controlling the BTS synchronization mode (e.g. hybrid sync, eCPRI master clock, SyncE generation), UTC offset validity checking, phase-error recovery thresholds, and manual frame-timing adjustment. It coordinates timing sources such as GNSS, PTP (TOPP), SyncE, and CLOCK inputs into the BTS's overall synchronization state.

SYNCE.description: Configures Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE) on a specific Ethernet link (ethlkDN), including SSM (Synchronization Status Message) handling — whether SSM is enabled, the minimum acceptable quality level, timeout behavior, and forced network re-arrangement on major SSM events. SyncE distributes a physical-layer frequency reference over Ethernet as an alternative/complement to GNSS or PTP.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8262/G.8264 Synchronous Ethernet), not 3GPP. Frequency distribution over Ethernet physical layer, unrelated to 3GPP.

SYNC_R.description: A runtime synchronization-quality status object reporting the BTS's absolute time error and local (relative) time error versus its reference clock, used to monitor whether the node's timing meets the accuracy required for TDD/NR frame alignment and other sync-sensitive functions.

TAC.description: A container object for Tracking Area Code definitions used by the eNodeB, under which per-TAC configuration (see LTAC) is defined. It has no parameters of its own and serves purely as a grouping/parent node.

threeGpp.note: Idle-mode mobility priorities, handover/redirect targets, and Tracking Area configuration are all broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

TEST.description: TEST appears to be a generic maintenance/diagnostic test object (with no directly configurable parameters observed), likely serving as a trigger or parent container for hardware test procedures whose outcomes are recorded in related objects such as RFRES.

threeGpp.note: Physical hardware modeling (cabinets, modules, cables, transceivers, etc.) at this granularity is Nokia's own equipment model -- 3GPP's Network Resource Model does not standardize individual hardware unit types.

TGTTHRESHPR.description: No curated description is available for managed object class "TGTTHRESHPR". It did not appear in the researched sample set. Based on Nokia RAN naming conventions, it is a managed object class in the SBTS/AirScale or Flexi Zone data model; the sample parameters it configures are listed below for context.

TIME.description: Configures the local time zone and daylight-saving-time (DST) transition rules for the site, including the UTC offset before and after a DST change and the date on which the change takes effect. It is a site-wide administrative object used to correctly timestamp logs, alarms, and PM data.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IANA Time Zone Database, not 3GPP. Timezone/DST rules are a general software convention (see the ~543-option tz database), not any telecom standards body's concern.

TMSWPR.description: TMSWPR (Transmission Mode Switch Profile) defines the CQI thresholds and prohibit/hysteresis timers that govern automatic switching between LTE MIMO transmission modes (e.g. TM3, TM7, TM8, TM9) based on measured channel quality, including specific thresholds for 256QAM-capable UEs and beamforming-related CQI thresholds.

threeGpp.note: Built on top of standardized concepts (PUCCH resource config / transmission mode, TS 36.331 and TS 36.213 respectively), but the load-based decision logic and thresholds in this specific profile are Nokia's own algorithm, not something 3GPP specifies.

TNL.description: The root container object for the Transport Network Layer configuration branch, holding a general usage-type tag and label. It is the parent for the site's Ethernet, IP, VLAN, routing, and QoS transport configuration objects (ETHLK, IPNO, VLANIF, IPRT, QOS, etc.).

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

TNLSVC.description: Has no configurable parameters of its own; it appears to represent a Transport Network Layer service container, likely grouping or representing a bundled transport service configuration under the TNL branch.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

TNL_R.description: A top-level transport-network-layer runtime/feature-status object reporting whether various transport features are active on the node: automatic X2/Xn mesh establishment, dynamic IPsec, fast IP re-routing, IPsec backup tunnels and packet-switched tunnels, and IPv4-based Iub/S1/X2 transport. It gives a consolidated view of which advanced transport capabilities are currently enabled.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

TOP.description: TOP is the top-level 'Timing over Packet' (PTP/IEEE 1588) synchronization object, referencing the S-plane IP address used for PTP messaging and the PTP domain number. It anchors the packet-timing configuration alongside the more specific TOPB (boundary clock) and TOPF (frequency sync) objects.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8271/G.8275 Telecom Profiles) and IEEE (1588 PTP), not 3GPP. 3GPP requires certain synchronization ACCURACY budgets for radio operation (e.g. TS 36.133/38.133), but does not itself define the PTP/eCPRI synchronization protocol used to achieve them.

TOPB.description: TOPB configures the 'Timing over Packet' Boundary Clock function (IEEE 1588 PTP), enabling the node to act as a boundary clock and/or a master clock towards downstream devices for packet-based frequency/phase synchronization.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8271/G.8275 Telecom Profiles) and IEEE (1588 PTP), not 3GPP. 3GPP requires certain synchronization ACCURACY budgets for radio operation (e.g. TS 36.133/38.133), but does not itself define the PTP/eCPRI synchronization protocol used to achieve them.

TOPF.description: TOPF configures Timing-over-Packet (PTP/IEEE 1588) frequency synchronization behavior, including the accepted clock quality, the telecom PTP profile in use, announce-message request mode, sync message logging interval, PTP domain number, and the list of candidate master clocks. It works alongside TOPB and TOP to establish packet-based timing references.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8271/G.8275 Telecom Profiles) and IEEE (1588 PTP), not 3GPP. 3GPP requires certain synchronization ACCURACY budgets for radio operation (e.g. TS 36.133/38.133), but does not itself define the PTP/eCPRI synchronization protocol used to achieve them.

TOPP.description: Configures a Precision Time Protocol (PTP, 'Timing over Packet') synchronization profile, including the accepted master clock class/quality, the list and priority of PTP master candidates, the PTP domain number, multicast address, and standard profile used. It underlies packet-based phase/time synchronization for the site, working alongside the SYNC and CLOCK objects.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8271/G.8275 Telecom Profiles) and IEEE (1588 PTP), not 3GPP. 3GPP requires certain synchronization ACCURACY budgets for radio operation (e.g. TS 36.133/38.133), but does not itself define the PTP/eCPRI synchronization protocol used to achieve them.

TOPP_R.description: A management-plane runtime object under the site management-network-layer branch, exposing only a reference to another managed object (targetDN). Its exact purpose could not be confidently determined from the limited data, but the naming and lone targetDN parameter suggest a pointer/status object linking to a related configuration or topology target, similar in pattern to CMP_R/CRLH_R/CMPECDSA_R.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the ITU-T (G.8271/G.8275 Telecom Profiles) and IEEE (1588 PTP), not 3GPP. 3GPP requires certain synchronization ACCURACY budgets for radio operation (e.g. TS 36.133/38.133), but does not itself define the PTP/eCPRI synchronization protocol used to achieve them.

TRACKINGAREA.description: TRACKINGAREA defines a 5G System Tracking Area, holding the 5GS Tracking Area Code (fiveGsTac) and the list of network slices (S-NSSAI, via snssaiList/snssaiDN) associated with that tracking area, used for mobility management (paging/registration areas) and network-slice-aware cell selection within the gNB's coverage.

threeGpp.note: NR idle-mode mobility and Tracking Area configuration are broadcast via 3GPP-defined SIB/RRC structures.

specs.title: NR; Radio Resource Control (RRC) protocol specification

TRBLCADM.description: The site-wide Troubleshooting Configuration Administration object, controlling diagnostic and logging features such as core-dump file collection, internal tracing, and remote syslog transmission, plus the timers/thresholds for automatic self-healing procedures like antenna- or PRACH-based sleeping-cell detection and recovery. It centralizes diagnostic and self-healing policy for the site.

threeGpp.note: A Nokia feature-configuration/administration wrapper; some of the underlying radio features it controls are 3GPP-standardized even where this specific object isn't -- check the individual parameters (phase 2 of this work) for those cases.

TRBLCADM_R.description: A troubleshooting/logging administration runtime object reporting the transmission status of remote syslog messages (remoteSyslogTransmissionStatus) from the BTS to a centralized log collector, used to verify that diagnostic/event logs are successfully being exported off the node.

threeGpp.note: Site-wide Nokia O&M/administrative configuration, not part of any 3GPP-defined model.

TRSNW.description: Represents a Transport Network selection/association object, used mainly in older Flexi Zone LTE configurations, that indicates which underlying IP transport network (identified by transportNwId) carries a cell's or interface's control-plane (cPlane) and user-plane (uPlane) traffic. It references a specific local IPv4 address (ipV4AddressDN1) and a flag showing whether that transport network is currently in use. It typically sits under an LTE cell or BTS transport-configuration branch, linking radio/logical objects to a concrete IP transport path.

threeGpp.note: General IP/Ethernet transport configuration -- governed by IETF/IEEE standards where a standard applies at all, not by 3GPP.

threeGpp.note: Standardized by the IETF (RFC 5357), not 3GPP. Two-Way Active Measurement Protocol is an IETF specification, not a 3GPP one, even though it's commonly used to measure a mobile backhaul's transport performance.
